title: Photonics Fabrication and Design Engineer
description:
**About Us**
------------


Great Sky is a technology startup based with a mission to rebuild AI from first principles. We are pursuing neuroscience\-inspired hardware and algorithms that overcome the greatest challenges in scaling AI systems.


**Job Overview**
----------------


We are seeking a highly motivated Photonics Fabrication and Design Engineer to develop the cryogenic photonic networks central to our technology platform. In this role, you will contribute to the design of SiN\-based passive photonic components and take full ownership of the R\&D prototyping lifecycle. You will perform hands\-on device fabrication at a cleanroom facility located near our Boulder office. This is a high\-ownership position with substantial influence on the pace and direction of our hardware development.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Own end\-to\-end prototype fabrication runs in a research cleanroom environment.
* Develop, execute, and optimize manufacturable fabrication processes for integrated photonic devices and superconducting devices, including SNSPDs.
* Design, simulate and optimize passive silicon nitride (SiN) photonic components such as (e.g., grating couplers, splitters, mode converters, edge couplers and optical I/O).
* Establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and process flows into stable Processes of Record (POR).
* Contribute to the development and maintenance of internal Process Design Kits (PDKs) and component libraries.
* Work closely with test, packaging, and systems integration teams to correlate device performance with fabrication metrics, accelerating our design\-build\-test\-learn cycles.

**Qualifications \& Skills**
----------------------------

**Required:**

* BS, MS or PhD in physics, electrical engineering, optics, materials science, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience.
* Hands\-on experience in microfabrication, nanofabrication, or semiconductor processing.
* Experience with fabricating devices on at least one of these platforms: silicon photonics, silicon nitride, and/or superconducting electronics.
* Strong background in passive photonic component design with proficiency in industry\-standard electromagnetic simulation software (e.g., Ansys Lumerical, Tidy3D).
* Solid understanding of photonic layout concepts, Design Rule Checking (DRC), and familiarity with standard layout tools (e.g., KLayout, Luceda, Cadence).

**Preferred:**

* Experience with SNSPD fabrication.
* Experience with heterogeneous or hybrid integration methods such as bump bonding or fusion bonding.
* Experience transferring processes to external fabs or working with foundries.
* Previous fabrication background utilizing shared, multi\-user facilities such as university cleanrooms, national laboratories, or advanced commercial R\&D centers.

**Benefits and Perks**
----------------------

* Meaningful equity ownership in an early\-stage deep tech company
* Employer\-matched 401(k)
* Health, dental, vision, and life insurance
* Flexible PTO
* Support for ongoing learning, conference attendance, and skill development


Our culture is onsite by default (we're founded by scientists who are used to working in the lab), with flexibility for hybrid arrangements. For the right person and role, we're open to filling roles remotely


Compensation Range: $140K \- $180K

title: Neuroimaging Research Data Analyst
description:
University Staff**Description**
---------------

 **University of Colorado Anschutz****Department: Psychiatry****Job Title:** **Neuroimaging Research Data Analyst****Position \#:00852958 – Requisition \#:** **41084**

 **Job Summary:**  

The Neuromoimaging Research Data Analyst will provide quantitative, computational, and data management support for a multidisciplinary neuromodulation research program within the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. The research program uses advanced neuroscience methods, including functional and structural magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI/MRI), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), neuronavigation, clinical assessments, behavioral measures, and other multimodal approaches to investigate brain circuitry and develop and evaluate neuromodulation interventions for psychiatric and related conditions.


Working as part of Neuromodulation Research, the Research Data Analyst will work under the Neuromodulation Chair, and in collaboration with faculty investigators, research professionals, clinicians, statisticians, data scientists, and trainees. The position will support the organization, processing, quality control, analysis, integration, visualization, and reporting of complex neuroimaging research datasets. Responsibilities will include implementation of established computational workflows, development and maintenance of research datasets and code, statistical and neuroimaging analyses, data quality assurance, preparation of research results, and support for manuscripts, presentations, and grant applications. The position will apply established quantitative methods while developing increasing independence and expertise in neuroimaging, neuromodulation, and reproducible research practices.  

Key Responsibilities:**25% – Research Data Processing and Quantitative Analysis**

* Process and analyze neuroimaging, neuromodulation, behavioral, clinical, and other research datasets using established quantitative and computational methods.
* Implement statistical analyses under the guidance of senior scientific personnel and investigators.
* Apply established analysis pipelines to functional and structural MRI data and other neuroscience datasets.
* Generate summary statistics, derived variables, quantitative measures, and analytic datasets for research projects.
* Assist with integration of imaging, TMS, neuronavigation, clinical, behavioral, and other multimodal research data.

**20% – Neuroimaging and Neuromodulation Data Analysis**

* Perform preprocessing and quality assessment of functional and structural MRI data using established software and analysis pipelines.
* Assist with analyses of brain structure, function, connectivity, and other imaging\-derived measures relevant to neuromodulation research.
* Support processing and analysis of data used for MRI\-informed TMS targeting and neuronavigation.
* Assist with quantitative evaluation of relationships among stimulation targets, imaging measures, treatment parameters, and clinical or behavioral outcomes.
* Identify data quality issues and consult with senior scientific personnel regarding appropriate resolution or exclusion procedures.

**15% – Research Data Management and Quality Assurance**

* Organize, maintain, and document research datasets according to program standards and approved research protocols.
* Perform routine data quality checks to identify missing, inconsistent, duplicated, out\-of\-range, or otherwise problematic data.
* Assist with development and maintenance of data dictionaries, variable definitions, file structures, metadata, and other research documentation.
* Reconcile information across research data sources and work with study personnel to resolve discrepancies.
* Support preparation of analysis\-ready datasets while maintaining appropriate participant confidentiality and data security.

**15% – Computational Workflows and Reproducible Research**

* Implement, maintain, and troubleshoot established computational workflows for research data processing and analysis.
* Write, modify, test, and document code and scripts using programming and scientific computing tools such as Python, R, MATLAB, shell scripting, or related platforms.
* Use version\-control and code\-management practices to support reproducibility and collaboration.
* Assist with automation of repetitive data processing, quality\-control, and reporting tasks.
* Maintain clear documentation of analytical procedures, software versions, processing parameters, and data transformations.

**10% – Statistical Analysis and Data Visualization**

* Conduct descriptive and inferential statistical analyses under the direction of investigators and senior quantitative personnel.
* Create tables, figures, dashboards, and other visualizations to communicate research findings and data quality metrics.
* Assist with interpretation of statistical and quantitative results in collaboration with the Neuromodulation Research Lead Scientist and study investigators.
* Support exploratory analyses and feasibility assessments for new research questions and grant applications.

**5% – Scientific Dissemination**

* Prepare figures, tables, data summaries, methods documentation, and other quantitative materials for manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, grant applications, progress reports, and scientific meetings.
* Assist investigators and senior scientific personnel with responding to data and analysis questions arising during manuscript and grant preparation.
* Maintain sufficient documentation to support verification and reproducibility of reported research findings.

**5% – Research Collaboration and Technical Support**

* Participate in Neuromodulation Research, research program, and individual study meetings as appropriate.
* Work collaboratively with investigators and research personnel to understand project requirements and translate research questions into defined data and analysis tasks.
* Provide technical assistance to research team members regarding established data management, processing, analysis, and visualization procedures.
* Coordinate with research informatics, information technology, imaging, and other institutional resources as needed to resolve routine data or computational issues.

**5% – Research Compliance and Professional Development**

* Conduct research data activities in accordance with approved protocols, data use requirements, institutional policies, and applicable human\-subjects research requirements.
* Maintain appropriate protections for confidential and sensitive research information.
* Complete required institutional research, information security, human\-subjects protection, MRI safety, and other applicable training.
* Maintain knowledge of evolving methods, software, and best practices relevant to neuroimaging, neuromodulation, quantitative neuroscience, and reproducible research.
* Perform other research data and quantitative support duties as assigned.
 **Work Location:**  

Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, CO. This position is expected to work at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, with hybrid work eligibility determined by the needs of the Department of Psychiatry, Neuromodulation Research Program, and Neuromodulation Research. **Why Join Us:**  

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus Department of Psychiatry is home to one of the most comprehensive neuromodulation programs in the country. Clinically, the department provides a full continuum of evidence\-based treatments, including transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) for obsessive\-compulsive disorder, Tourette Syndrome, depression, and chronic pain, Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT), and esketamine. This robust clinical infrastructure creates unparalleled opportunities for translational research directly tied to patient care.  

Our neuromodulation research portfolio is rapidly expanding, with active studies in TMS, DBS, and low\-intensity focused ultrasound, alongside initiatives in adaptive/closed\-loop stimulation and biomarker discovery. **Why work for the University?**  

We have AMAZING benefits and offerexceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:* Medical: Multiple plan options
* Dental: Multiple plan options
* Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision
* Retirement 401(a) Plan: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay
* Paid Time Off: Accruals over the year
* Vacation Days: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)

* Holiday Days: 15/year
* Tuition Benefit: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses

There are many additional perks \& programs with the CU Advantage. **Qualifications:** **Minimum Qualifications:*** Bachelor’s degree in social/behavioral sciences, physical sciences, public health, healthcare, or a directly related field from an accredited institution.
* 2 years of professional experience in research data analysis, quantitative research, neuroimaging, neuroscience research, biomedical data analysis, statistics, data science, scientific computing, or a closely related area relevant to the work assignment.
	+ *A combination of education and related technical, military, or paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year\-for\-year basis.*
	+ *An advanced degree (Master’s or Doctorate) may be substituted for experience on a year\-for\-year basis if the degree is in a field of study directly related to the work assignment.*

 *Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.***Preferred Qualifications:*** Experience analyzing human neuroscience, neuroimaging, clinical research, behavioral, or other complex biomedical research data.
* Experience with functional and/or structural MRI data processing and analysis and commonly used neuroimaging software or computational workflows.
* Experience using one or more programming or statistical languages such as Python, R, MATLAB, or related scientific computing tools.
* Experience with research data management, quality assurance, reproducible analysis workflows, and version\-control tools such as Git.
* Experience working in a multidisciplinary academic research environment and contributing quantitative analyses, figures, or other materials to scientific manuscripts, presentations, or grant applications.

 **Conditions of Employment:**

* This position is expected to work at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, with hybrid work eligibility determined by the needs of the Department of Psychiatry, Neuromodulation Research Program, and Neuromodulation Research.
* The position may require work in or around MRI, TMS, computational research, and clinical research environments.
* Must complete and maintain applicable institutional human\-subjects protection, information security, research compliance, MRI safety, and other required training.
* Must adhere to institutional requirements for access, storage, analysis, transmission, and protection of confidential and sensitive research data.
* Occasional schedule flexibility may be required to support research deadlines, data acquisition, grant submissions, or scientific activities.
* Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.

 **Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:*** **Quantitative and analytical skills:** Knowledge of quantitative research methods and ability to organize, process, analyze, interpret, and visualize complex research data using appropriate statistical and computational methods.
* **Computational skills:** Ability to use programming, statistical, and/or scientific computing tools to implement data\-processing and analysis workflows and to learn new analytical tools and methods as research needs evolve.
* **Data quality and reproducibility:** Ability to identify and resolve data quality issues, maintain accurate research documentation, and follow reproducible data management and analytical practices.
* **Problem\-solving and attention to detail:** Strong analytical reasoning and attention to detail, with the ability to troubleshoot routine data and computational problems and recognize when issues require consultation or escalation.
* **Communication:** Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally, and to explain data, analytical methods, and results to colleagues with varying levels of quantitative expertise.
* **Collaboration and customer service:** Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with faculty, scientists, clinicians, research staff, trainees, and employees at all levels throughout the institution, with outstanding customer service skills.
* **Organization and professional accountability:** Ability to manage multiple research assignments, meet project deadlines, maintain confidential information, and exercise appropriate discretion and personal accountability in a collaborative research environment.

title: Lead Animal Technician, Neuroscience
description:
**Job Summary:**

The lead research technician assists Neuroscience personnel in coordinating efforts on the day\-to\-day operations of active studies. They assist Study Directors (SDs) and Study Coordinators in accurately and efficiently conducting animal studies and supervise in\-life study execution, clinical observations, and treatments to ensure compliance with policies and procedures. They also provide leadership, training, and technical oversight to more junior technicians.

**Primary Responsibilities:**

* Directly works with the in\-vivo group to conduct required study activities.
* Assist SDs and Study Coordinators to ensure study protocol, schedules, formulations, and sample collections are correct and properly communicated to the research team.
* Assists Study Coordinators with the creation or verification of cage cards, sample collection prep labels, and data files.
* Read and understand IACUC protocols, SOPs, and all study protocols, demonstrating familiarity with critical timepoints
* Assists in disease induction procedures.
* Administer doses of compounds to rats and mice via common dosing routes, including but not limited to oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, and intraperitoneal.
* Perform data collections, including weighing, clinical observations, health assessments, post operative monitoring, and disease progression scoring.
* Perform blood collections from rats and mice via tail vein, retro\-orbital, and terminal blood draws and process these samples via centrifugation for plasma and/or serum.
* Perform behavioral testing (e.g. Cognitive, Motor, Mood, Von Frey, etc.) and *in vitro* work. Train other technicians in these areas as needed.
* Review facility schedules, dose formulation calculations, cage cards, spreadsheets, and study protocols for consistency and accuracy before the first dose event
* Review live phase data on all active studies for consistency and accuracy
* Assist in formulating experimental compounds for administration.
* Maintain study\-related forms (*e.g.* data sheets, health assessments, found dead forms, and moribund forms)
* Independently perform tissue collections and dosing after training with SD
* Assist with the preparation and execution of necropsies, tissue collection (terminal and interim) and surgeries for the Neuroscience department
* Keep laboratory clean and maintain inventory of all team supplies (*e.g.* media, plates, reagents, surgical tools, etc.) and study\-specific test articles.
* Supports and participates in other duties and company initiatives as directed
* Various software applications sustained by a Windows platform. (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)
* Use of general laboratory equipment, including but not limited to balances, syringes and needles, blood collection tubes, centrifuges, pipettes, formalin collection jars, liquid nitrogen, \-80 freezers, incubators, fluid/syringe pumps, chemical and clean hoods, PPE (lab coat, gloves, face mask or respirator, shoe covers, hair nets, eye protection), quarantine/isolation rooms, autoclaves, and necropsy hand tools.
* Other tasks as assigned

**Education \& Experience:**

* M.S./B.S./B.A. in science (biology or equivalent; neuroscience preferred) with 1\-3 years of direct animal behavioral work experience, or Associate degree with 4 years direct laboratory animal work experience, or 6 years of direct laboratory animal work experience without a college science degree, or equivalent combination of related education and required work experience will be considered with management approval.
* Animal laboratory research experience with mice and rats, including dosing, in\-life sample collections, and necropsy collections.
* Preferred experience in neuroscience disease area research, including behavioral assessments, stereotaxic surgery in rodents, and neuroanatomy.

**Skills \& Abilities:**

* Demonstrates a working knowledge and awareness of general laboratory procedures.
* Demonstrates an ability to follow detailed instructions, work independently, and work in a team environment.
* Demonstrates an ability to use computer software to compile and maintain study data and reports for study records and sample inventory.
* Demonstrates a positive attitude and respect for co\-workers, managers, and other employees.
* Exhibits a basic understanding of GLP, AAALAC, OLAW, USDA, OHS, PHS, The Guide, and IACUC regulations and standards with consistent application of these practices.
* Exhibits accuracy performing laboratory operations.
* Exhibits an aptitude for quality, an eye for detail, the ability to follow written instructions and work with a minimum of supervision.
* Exhibits good written and oral communication skills and suitable organization skills
* Maintains a commitment to adhere to all safety regulations and procedures.

* This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience. This is a non\-exempt role paying $25\-$27/hour and can adjust along with the level of the role to match the person’s relevant experience and/or education level.

* *This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience. The salary range will adjust along with the level of the role to match the person’s relevant experience and/or education level.*

 *At Inotiv, our work helps advance the development of new medicines and therapies that can improve people's lives. As a leading global contract research organization (CRO), we partner with researchers to tackle complex scientific challenges, drive innovation, and help build a healthier, safer world. Bringing together scientists, researchers, technical experts, and business professionals, we provide the expertise and collaboration needed to move research forward. description:
Faculty**Description**
---------------

 **University of Colorado Anschutz**

**Department:** **Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences**

**Job Title:** **Postdoctoral Fellow – In Vivo Pharmacology and Translational Oncology**

**Position \#00804247 – Requisition \#41112**

**Job Summary:**

  

A full\-time Postdoctoral Fellow position is available in the laboratory of Professor Dan LaBarbera, PhD, within the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. We are seeking a highly motivated scientist with strong expertise in in vivo pharmacology, preclinical oncology, and mouse therapeutic efficacy studies to contribute to a federally funded translational research program focused on the preclinical development of novel small\-molecule therapeutics for colorectal cancer.


The research is conducted in collaboration with Onconaut Therapeutics Inc. and provides an opportunity to work at the interface of academic drug discovery, biotechnology, and translational oncology. The successful candidate will have substantial hands\-on experience designing and executing mouse efficacy studies, including cell line\-derived xenograft (CDX) and patient\-derived xenograft (PDX) models. The position requires proficiency in mouse handling and welfare and in repeated drug administration by oral gavage, intraperitoneal injection, and intravenous tail\-vein injection. Experience with orthotopic colorectal cancer models is highly desirable.


Key Responsibilities:

* Design, plan, and execute in vivo pharmacology and therapeutic efficacy studies in mouse models of colorectal cancer.
* Establish and conduct cell line\-derived xenograft (CDX) and patient\-derived xenograft (PDX) studies, including tumor implantation, growth monitoring, randomization, treatment, and study endpoints.
* Administer investigational therapeutics using multiple routes, including oral gavage (PO), intraperitoneal injection (IP), and intravenous tail\-vein injection (IV), including repeated\-dose treatment regimens.
* Perform routine mouse handling and health monitoring in both male and female mice, including restraint, body\-weight and condition assessment, precise tumor measurements, and implementation of appropriate humane endpoints.
* Collect blood, tumors, and other tissues; perform or coordinate necropsy and tissue processing; and support downstream histologic, molecular, and pharmacodynamic/target\-engagement analyses.
* Analyze and interpret experimental data, maintain accurate study records, and prepare figures, presentations, reports, manuscripts, and other scientific materials.
* Collaborate with academic and industry investigators to develop experimental protocols, interpret results, troubleshoot studies, and advance preclinical therapeutic development.
 **Work Location:**

  

Onsite – This role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, Colorado, at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus.


Because animal pharmacology studies require treatment and monitoring according to experimental schedules, occasional work outside standard business hours, including evenings or weekends, may be required.

 **Why Join Us:**

  

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus provides an outstanding environment for translational biomedical research, with extensive expertise and infrastructure in drug discovery, cancer biology, pharmacology, animal models, imaging, and therapeutic development. The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences and the CU Anschutz Center for Drug Discovery provide a multidisciplinary research environment spanning discovery through preclinical development.


This position offers a unique opportunity to participate directly in an industry\-academic translational drug development program in collaboration with Onconaut Therapeutics Inc. The fellow will gain substantial experience in preclinical oncology pharmacology and the advancement of investigational therapeutics toward clinical development, providing excellent preparation for careers in biotechnology, pharmaceutical R\&D, translational research, or academia.


The University of Colorado offers a comprehensive benefits package. To see what benefits are available for Post\-Doctoral Fellows, please visit:

* Payroll \& Benefits Orientation for Post\-Doctoral Fellows \| University of Colorado (CU.edu)
* Benefits Guide for Post\-Doctoral Fellows (CU.edu)
 **Qualifications:**

 **Minimum Qualifications:**

*Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.*

* PhD, MD, DVM, or equivalent doctoral degree in pharmacology, pharmaceutical sciences, cancer biology, molecular or cellular biology, translational biomedical sciences, or a closely related field.
* Demonstrated hands\-on experience designing and conducting mouse in vivo pharmacology or therapeutic efficacy studies.
* Demonstrated experience with mouse tumor xenograft models, including cell line\-derived xenografts and patient\-derived xenografts.
* Demonstrated proficiency in mouse handling, restraint, health monitoring, and animal welfare procedures.
* Demonstrated proficiency administering drugs to mice by oral gavage, intraperitoneal injection, and intravenous tail\-vein injection.
* Experience independently collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and documenting data from animal studies.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience designing and conducting preclinical oncology efficacy studies with investigational small\-molecule therapeutics.
* Experience establishing, expanding, and conducting therapeutic studies using patient\-derived xenograft models.
* Experience with orthotopic tumor models, particularly colorectal or gastrointestinal cancer models.
* Experience with surgical or microsurgical procedures used to establish orthotopic mouse tumor models.
* Experience with immunodeficient mouse strains commonly used for oncology studies.
* Experience with blood collection, necropsy, tumor and organ harvest, tissue processing, and preparation of samples for histologic and molecular analyses.
* Experience with pharmacodynamic or target\-engagement studies in tumor tissues, including techniques such as Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and/or immunofluorescence.
* Evidence of scientific productivity through peer\-reviewed publications and/or scientific presentations.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

* Strong knowledge of in vivo pharmacology, experimental oncology, and therapeutic efficacy study design.
* Strong technical skills in mouse handling and drug administration.
* Knowledge of animal welfare, humane endpoints, and principles governing responsible vertebrate animal research.
* Ability to independently design rigorous, reproducible animal experiments and troubleshoot experimental problems.
* Strong quantitative, analytical, and scientific data interpretation skills.
* Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage complex longitudinal studies involving multiple treatment groups and dosing schedules.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills.
* Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary academic and industry research team.
* Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate experimental documentation.

**Conditions of Employment:** This position requires regular onsite work with research animals and participation in applicable institutional animal\-care, training, and occupational\-health programs. Experimental schedules may require work outside standard business hours, including evenings and weekends.

title: Research Scientist
description:
Research Faculty**Description**
---------------

 **University of Colorado Anschutz**

**Department of Pediatrics \| Section of Neonatology**

**Job Title: Research Scientist**

**Position \#:** **00848028 – Requisition \#:41116**

**Job Summary:**

  

The candidate will support a basic\-translational research program focused on lung biology by analyzing high\-throughput sequencing data, including bulk RNA\-seq, single\-cell RNA\-seq, and spatial transcriptomics, to investigate gene expression and cellular dynamics in lung development and disease. This role involves close collaboration with bench scientists to design experiments, interpret biological data, and translate complex datasets into actionable scientific insights. The bioinformatician will develop and maintain reproducible computational pipelines, generate clear visualizations and reports, and ensure data integrity across all stages of analysis. The position requires both independent problem\-solving and active engagement with the broader research team to advance the lab's scientific goals.


Key Responsibilities:

* Design, conduct, and lead independent and collaborative biomedical research projects focused on pulmonary biology, neonatal lung injury, and translational medicine.
* Analyze and interpret complex multiomics datasets, including bulk RNA sequencing, single\-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA\-seq), and spatial transcriptomics data using R, Python, and advanced bioinformatics methodologies.
